name: cloud-superapp-mcp
description: MCP + HTTP faces over the Android constellation's on-device debug API (libs:devtools AppDebugServer, behind the SuperApp mesh gateway), reached over ssh. lib-api/lib-mcp shared, one module per app under mcps-apps/, one server process.

native_build._cmd_doc: npm install, not npm ci: this monorepo has no committed package-lock.json.
native_build._apt_doc: device.ts spawns ssh to reach the phone's loopback-bound SuperApp mesh gateway (127.0.0.1:38080, /app/<pkg>/api/<op>, every app behind it over Android IPC), or a pre-gateway app's own port.
native_build._user_doc: root so the /root/.ssh key mount is readable, same as cloud-infra-mcp.

ssh._extra_hosts_doc: Ssh aliases the MCP dials (SUPERAPP_HOSTS in src/compose.nix). The phone's sshd is provided by OUR terminals (cloud-u-android ac_cloud-nix-on-droid / ac_cloud-termux; ports and users as declared in ac_cloud-myterminal/data/terminal-targets.json: nix 8024 user nix-on-droid, termux 8023 user termux). Address = the phone's wg0 mesh client `termux` (config.json native.wireguard.clients), resolved by the derive into /opt/ssh-keys/cloud-superapp-mcp/config. MESH ONLY: the phone has no public ssh route by design (sshd is reached over WireGuard; ide-endpoints.json: public surface is 443+51820+25), so there is no phone-pub. The key offered is vault_id_rsa (keys above); it is authorised on the phone by cloud-u-linux da__my-konsole/termux/authorized_keys. test-superapp-hosts.sh fails if an alias in SUPERAPP_HOSTS has no entry here.

mcp.description: Discovers every constellation app behind the phone's SuperApp mesh gateway (127.0.0.1:38080 /api/fleet/apps, each app at /app/<pkg>/api/<op> over Android IPC; a pre-gateway phone's apps on 38090-38389) and proxies its routes: logcat, crashes, docs, fleet wake, and any app-registered route via superapp_call. App aliases come from mcps-apps/<id>/, so cloud-mail resolves without asking the device.
mcp._doc_stdio: How .mcp.json should launch this. Through mcp-local-launch.sh, not `npm start`: the entry is cloud-superapp-mcp/src/index.ts but it imports ../../lib-mcp/src/, and Node walks up from the IMPORTING file — so a node_modules beside the entry alone leaves lib-mcp and every mcps-apps module unresolved (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on the SDK). The launcher links the solution root, which the walk reaches from all of them, and self-heals if it is missing or dangling. Run through `sh -c` so ${VAR:-default} is expanded by a shell we know does it — the same trick headersHelper already uses in that file. MCP_LOCAL_LAUNCH and CLOUD_INFRA_DIR override the two paths.
